headline: High: Copilot can read and write repo/editor context while the paired course profile has no isolation, creating default-path data leakage and cascading misapplication risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot ingests editor open buffers and repo context by default, so malicious instructions in shared content could influence its outputs. The zoomcamp profile is a course repo with no isolation or countermeasure shown, so if its materials are fed into Copilot, prompt-like text could be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b editor buffers or repo context, injection risk exists.
IF agent_b treats file text as instruction-bearing content, malicious prompts in agent_a materials can steer outputs.
mitigations: Restrict Copilot to trusted files only.
Remove instruction-like text from shared course materials.
Use a separate review buffer for untrusted content.
Disable Workspace edits for untrusted repos.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between course content and assistant context.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot reads open buffers and repo context and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com, while the zoomcamp profile is an open-source course repo with no stated data controls. If sensitive notes or secrets are placed in the shared workspace, Copilot can transmit them off-host. The course profile does not itself show sensitive data, so this is a default-path leakage risk rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF sensitive material is placed in the repo or editor buffers, Copilot can ingest it.
IF Copilot requests are sent to api.githubcopilot.com, that material leaves the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use a redacted copy of course materials.
Turn off Copilot for sensitive files.
Review editor buffers before enabling chat.
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning and context filtering.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while the zoomcamp profile is a course repository with no write-capability surface shown. There is overlap only if both are pointed at the same repo, and the concurrency model for the course profile is absent. This suggests possible edit contention, but the blast radius is limited to repository state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF agent_b applies Workspace edits while agent_a content is being updated, git state may diverge.
mitigations: Use one editor session at a time.
Commit or stash before Copilot applies edits.
Work on a branch per agent.
Review diffs before merge.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared repo writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot’s Workspace and chat can propose or apply edits from repo context, so if zoomcamp materials are treated as authoritative, downstream code or documentation may be changed based on unverified course content. The course profile is not an action-taking agent, but its content can still seed Copilot’s outputs. The pathway is plausible in default editor workflows.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a materials as source context, Copilot may propagate their claims into edits.
IF human reviewers accept Workspace suggestions without verification, errors cascade into the repo.
mitigations: Verify claims against primary sources.
Require human review of every suggested edit.
Limit Copilot to formatting-only tasks.
Annotate untrusted course-derived facts.
requires-engineering: add citation checks before applying edits.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is shown for either profile, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch evidenced. Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context, while the zoomcamp profile is an open-source course repo; the only compliance concern is generic policy mismatch if regulated data is later introduced. The other agent is not cited because no regulated data flow is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is added to the shared repo or buffers, compliance review is required.
IF organizational policy forbids third-party processing of repo context, Copilot use becomes noncompliant.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Confirm vendor approval for Copilot.
Use a non-sensitive test repo.
Review retention settings in GitHub.
requires-engineering: implement data-class gating for assistant context.
